When the emperor and empress were about to visit Cixiao Temple together, they wanted the great imperial palanquin to go ahead carrying the late emperor's spirit tablet. Zongdao said: "When a husband dies, a wife follows her son—that is the proper order for a woman."

When the emperor and empress dowager were about to visit Cixiao Temple together, they wanted the Da'an palanquin to go ahead of the emperor. Zongdao said: "When a husband dies, a wife follows her son—that is the proper order for a woman."
太后 is the empress dowager; 大安輦 is the Da'an palanquin; 先帝行 means going ahead of the emperor, as 輦后乘輿 in the next sentence confirms, not a late emperor's tablet.
He was again transferred to vice minister of rites in the Ministry of Revenue and commissioner of Xiangyuan Temple.
He was again transferred to vice minister of rites and commissioner of Xiangyuan Abbey.
尚書禮部侍郎 belongs to the Ministry of Rites, not Revenue; 祥源觀 is an abbey (觀), not a Buddhist temple.

Several months later he was recalled as supervisory commissioner of Shaanzhou, made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, vice transport commissioner of Huainan, then commissioner for Jiang-Huai transport and grain distribution.

Several months later he was recalled as controller-general (tongpan) of Shaanzhou, made vice director of the Ministry of Revenue, vice transport commissioner of Huainan, then commissioner for Jiang-Huai transport and grain distribution.
通判陝州 is tongpan of Shaanzhou, not a supervisory commissioner.

Within the year he accumulated three million bushels of grain, three million in tax surplus, verified several thousand qing of concealed private fields, and obtained more than a hundred thousand bundles of fodder.

Within the year he accumulated three million bushels of grain, thirty million in tax surplus, verified several thousand qing of concealed private fields, and obtained more than a hundred thousand bundles of fodder.
征算餘三千萬 is a tax surplus of thirty million, not three million.
He was transferred to vice minister of rites in the Ministry of Revenue.
He was transferred to vice minister of rites in the Ministry of Rites.
尚書禮部侍郎 is vice minister in the Ministry of Rites, not Revenue.

Many chief ministers of the two councils had already been dismissed. Kui developed asthma, repeatedly asked to resign, and was relieved as vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.

Many chief ministers of the two councils had already been dismissed. Kui developed asthma, repeatedly asked to resign, and was relieved of his council post to serve as vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.
罷為 introduces the offices conferred when he left his council seat, not offices he was stripped of.

At the time many chief ministers of the two councils had been dismissed; Kui contracted asthma and repeatedly asked to resign, and was dismissed as vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.

At the time many chief ministers of the two councils had been dismissed; Kui contracted asthma and repeatedly asked to resign, and was dismissed to become vice minister of revenue, academician of the Zizheng Hall, and director of the Secretariat's general office.
罷為 means he was moved into these posts on resignation, not dismissed from them.
Kui's nature was stern and he would not compromise; on affairs he dared speak out. In Emperor Zhenzong's time he often banqueted the chief ministers, and some even became drunk.
Kui's nature was stern and he would not compromise; on affairs he dared speak out. In Emperor Zhenzong's time the emperor often banqueted the chief ministers, and some even became drunk.
真宗時數宴大臣 makes Zhenzong the host; Kui's following remonstrance to 陛下 confirms the emperor gave the banquets.
His family long dwelt in the Fen and Fen region and later became people of Henan.
His family long dwelt in the He-Fen region and later became people of Henan.
河汾 is the He-Fen (Yellow River and Fen) region, not a duplicated Fen.

For recommending a jinshi candidate inaccurately he was demoted to supervisor of Luzhou tea tax, then again transferred to vice director of works in the Ministry of Revenue and awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

For recommending a jinshi candidate inaccurately he was demoted to supervisor of Luzhou tea tax, then again transferred to vice director of works in the Ministry of Works and awaiting academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
尚書工部員外郎 belongs to the Ministry of Works, not Revenue.
When Kou Zhun was demoted again, Shu was demoted to military training vice commissioner of Ezhou.
When Kou Zhun was demoted again, Shu was demoted to military training vice commissioner of Yingzhou.
郢州 is Yingzhou, not Ezhou (鄂州).
When Zhun was demoted again, Shu was also demoted to military training vice commissioner of Ezhou.
When Zhun was demoted again, Shu was also demoted to military training vice commissioner of Yingzhou.
郢州 is Yingzhou, not Ezhou.
When the Chonghua Hall of Wei burned, Gao Tanglong took a single pavilion as a warning and advised stopping repair; Emperor Wen did not listen, and the next year it burned again.
When the Chonghua Hall of Wei burned, Gao Tanglong took terraces and palace buildings as a warning and advised stopping repair; Emperor Wen did not listen, and the next year it burned again.
壹榭宮室 is the 臺榭宮室 warning against lavish terraces and palaces; Sanguozhi Gao Tanglong reads 臺榭宮室為誡, not a single pavilion.
As vice minister of works in the Ministry of Revenue he became Vice Grand Councilor.
As vice minister of works he became Vice Grand Councilor.
尚書工部侍郎 is vice minister of works; Revenue is a mistranslation of 工部.
He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).
He was posthumously made Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).
中書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not Grand Preceptor (太師).
Posthumously made Grand Guardian and Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).
Posthumously made Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous title Wenkang (Cultured and Tranquil).
中書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat.
Tranquil by nature, he admired Tang Wang Guizhi and several times resigned to care for his parents.
Tranquil by nature, he admired Tang Wang Gui and several times resigned to care for his parents.
慕唐王龜之為人 names Tang Wang Gui; 之為人 is the idiom “as a person,” not a name 龜之.
After completing mourning he retired as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's gate office and often traveled with Buddhists and recluses through Luoyang's famous gardens, mountains, and rivers.
After completing mourning he retired as vice director of the Bureau of Gates and often traveled with Buddhists and recluses through Luoyang's famous gardens, mountains, and rivers.
尚書司門員外郎 is vice director of the Bureau of Gates, not a Ministry of Revenue gate office.

After his father's mourning ended he retired as vice director in the Ministry of Revenue's gate office, and from time to time traveled with Buddhists and recluses; famous gardens, mountains, and rivers of Luoyang—none he did not visit.

After his father's mourning ended he retired as vice director of the Bureau of Gates, and from time to time traveled with Buddhists and recluses; famous gardens, mountains, and rivers of Luoyang—none he did not visit.
尚書司門員外郎 is the Bureau of Gates, not a Revenue ministry post.
Yirou asked that two talented men be presented at once; public opinion warmly praised the change.
Yirou asked that as few as two men be presented at once; public opinion warmly praised the change.
才二人 means as few as two candidates, not two talented men; the proposed “once there were only two men” is still awkward.
Such as Li Yifu of Emperor Gaozong of Tang, Li Linfu of Emperor Ming of Tang, Lu Qi of Emperor Dezong, and Huangfu Bo of Emperor Xian of Tang—the mirrors of emperors.
Such as Li Yifu of Emperor Gaozong of Tang, Li Linfu of Minghuang, Lu Qi of Emperor Dezong, and Huangfu Bo of Emperor Xianzong of Tang—the mirrors of emperors.
明皇 is Minghuang, not Emperor Ming; 憲宗 is Xianzong, not a clipped Emperor Xian.
yet Ming and Xian were intelligent and were still so blinded by two men.
yet Minghuang and Xianzong were intelligent and were still so blinded by two men.
明皇 and 憲宗 are Minghuang and Xianzong; clipped Ming and Xian misidentify the rulers.
His intent plainly targeted Wang Anshi.
His intent presumably targeted Wang Anshi.
意蓋指 marks a historian's presumption, not certainty that the memorial “plainly” targeted Wang Anshi.
A rumor spread that Prince Jing Wang Yuanyan was commander-in-chief of all armies. The source was arrested and many were implicated.
A rumor spread that Prince Jing, Yuanyan, was commander-in-chief of all armies. The source was arrested and many were implicated.
荊王元儼 is Prince Jing, Yuanyan; stacking English Prince with Chinese wang is a naming error.

The next year he compiled the imperial diary, drafted edicts, judged the mobile selection office, became Tianzhang awaiting academician and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng circuits, and was promoted to direct Longtu academician for supplying the Hexi army.

The next year he compiled the imperial diary, drafted edicts, judged the mobile selection office, became Tianzhang awaiting academician and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng circuits, and was promoted to direct Longtu academician for supplying the Xihe army.
熙河 is the Xihe circuit, not Hexi (河西).

The next year he jointly compiled the imperial diary, was direct appointee of the Drafting Office and judge of the mobile selection office, appointed awaiting academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng and other circuits; for merit in supplying the Hexi army he was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

The next year he jointly compiled the imperial diary, was direct appointee of the Drafting Office and judge of the mobile selection office, appointed awaiting academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and overall transport commissioner of Qinfeng and other circuits; for merit in supplying the Xihe army he was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.
熙河 is Xihe, not Hexi.
A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited general Jing Sil to welcome him.
A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited general Jing Sili to welcome him.
景思立 is Jing Sili; dropping the final syllable yields a wrong personal name.
Yanqing ordered no one to go out rashly: even merit would not save disobedience. Sil went anyway and was defeated and killed.
Yanqing ordered no one to go out rashly: even merit would not save disobedience. Sili went anyway and was defeated and killed.
思立 is the given name Sili, not Sil.
A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited the great general Jing Sil to come welcome him.
A tribal officer falsely claimed Muzheng wished to surrender and invited the great general Jing Sili to come welcome him.
景思立 is Jing Sili; the literal line likewise dropped the final syllable.
Yanqing ordered that none go out rashly; even if one disobeyed regulations yet had merit he would still be executed. Sil did not obey and in the end was defeated and died.
Yanqing ordered that none go out rashly; even if one disobeyed regulations yet had merit he would still be executed. Sili did not obey and in the end was defeated and died.
思立 is Sili, matching 景思立.
candidateDispositions: Shu Road is a transport route.
People of Shu, a regional designation.
劉氏 ancestral temples, the Liu house, not an individual
Gloss of the posthumous title Jiansu.
Gloss of the posthumous title Jiansu.
Phrase containing the reign name already surfaced as Zhenzong.
Fragment of the examination name 賢良方正科.
萬言 is a quantity of writing, not a name
Gloss of the posthumous title Jiansu.
Gloss of the posthumous title Jiansu.
Gloss of the posthumous title Jiansu.
天子 here is the emperor's ceremonial robe, not a person mention.
天子 here is the emperor's ceremonial robe, not a person mention.

unresolvedReferences.description: The Khitan empress dowager whom southern envoys reportedly saw is not named.
The adopted heir (從子) and his biological father are not named.
The chief minister who dismissed Yirou is unnamed.
Which empress dowager is Wang Qixiong's affinal kin is not restated.
Personal names of the Chen father and daughter are not given.
Sima Guang's remark is dated only by his already having written the Comprehensive Mirror.
Liu Yan's dismissal and restoration have no owned calendar year beyond Cai Qi's youth.
Cai Qi's death year is not stated in owned units; Yansi's birth is only posthumous relative to that death.
Wang Shu's own career dates are not given in owned units.
The unnamed father of Cai Yanqing is an inferred kinship intermediary without an owned activity date.
